feed.title: Networking & Sysadmin — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome Arch
entry.summary: A list of Arch Linux–based distributions and projects.

entry.title: Awesome eBPF
entry.summary: A resource list for eBPF, which runs safe programs inside the kernel.

entry.title: Awesome GNOME
entry.summary: A list of apps and extensions for the GNOME desktop environment.

entry.title: Awesome IPFS
entry.summary: A list of tools and projects for IPFS, the decentralised file protocol.

entry.title: Awesome KDE
entry.summary: A list of apps and resources for the KDE desktop environment.

entry.title: Awesome Scapy
entry.summary: A list of tools and examples for Scapy, the Python packet-manipulation library. Unlike general network lists it centres on crafting and sending packets by hand.

entry.title: Awesome Windows
entry.summary: A list of the best apps and tools for the Windows desktop.

entry.title: Lokinet
entry.summary: A decentralised, IP-based onion-routing network that anonymises traffic across staked nodes. Unlike Tor it carries any IP protocol, not just web: a full overlay network on top of onion routing rather than a single application.

entry.title: Check Point Eğitim
entry.summary: The CCSA and CCSE certifications. What differs from other firewall vendors is that Check Point’s management architecture is its own body of knowledge — centralised policy management sits at the centre of the training.

entry.title: Cisco Sertifikasyon
entry.summary: The networking certification programme from CCNA to CCIE. Unlike vendor-neutral certificates it is specific to Cisco equipment; even so, CCNA is widely treated as a solid networking fundamentals curriculum regardless of vendor.

entry.title: Fortinet Training Institute
entry.summary: The NSE programme and security training. Against other vendor programmes most of it has been made free — the broadest no-cost resource for firewall and network security fundamentals.

entry.title: Juniper Sertifikasyon
entry.summary: Junos-based networking certifications. Against Cisco’s programme the entry-level exams have long been offered free and the training material is open — the no-cost route into networking.

entry.title: Linux Professional Institute
entry.summary: Distribution-neutral Linux certifications (LPIC-1, LPIC-2). Against Red Hat’s programme it is not tied to one distribution — this is the certificate that still applies if you run Debian, SUSE or Arch.

entry.title: Palo Alto Networks Eğitim
entry.summary: PCNSA and PCNSE certifications with firewall and cloud security training. Against Fortinet it targets the upper enterprise segment — the certificate pays off directly at organisations running those products.

entry.title: Red Hat Sertifikasyon
entry.summary: The RHCSA and RHCE certifications. Unlike multiple-choice vendor exams these are entirely practical — you complete tasks on a live system, which is why they carry weight on the Linux side.

entry.title: Asahi Linux
entry.summary: A project bringing mainline Linux to Apple Silicon Macs, reverse-engineering the GPU driver and power management. Unlike a virtual machine it runs on the metal, so you get the M-series chip’s full performance.

entry.title: CanYouSeeMe
entry.summary: A minimal check for whether a given port is reachable from outside. Unlike scanning locally it looks in from the internet, which is the only way to tell whether router port forwarding actually works.

entry.title: ICANN Lookup
entry.summary: Domain registration lookup through ICANN’s own interface. Against third-party WHOIS sites there are no ads and no sales pitch — you do not get an email the next day about the domain you looked up.

entry.title: ntop
entry.summary: A family of tools for real-time network traffic monitoring, showing which device moves how much over which protocol. Where Wireshark inspects packet by packet, this watches the flow continuously — for noticing the anomaly rather than dissecting it.

entry.title: OpenSpeedTest
entry.summary: A browser-based speed test needing no Flash and no app, and self-hostable on your own server. That self-hosting is the difference from Speedtest.net: you can measure your LAN’s real throughput without an internet hop.

entry.title: Tailscale
entry.summary: A mesh VPN on top of WireGuard that connects your devices directly even behind NAT and firewalls. Unlike a classic VPN server there is no central exit hop: traffic goes device to device and the coordination server only hands out keys.

entry.title: Advanced Bash-Scripting Guide
entry.summary: The most comprehensive free reference on Bash scripting, every topic with a runnable example. Dated in style, still unmatched in coverage.

entry.title: Bash Guide for Beginners
entry.summary: An introduction to shell scripting that lays the groundwork without the weight of the advanced guide.

entry.title: Bash Referans Kılavuzu
entry.summary: Bash’s official manual — the final word on contested topics like expansion rules and parameter substitution.

entry.title: BashGuide (Wooledge)
entry.summary: A corrective to the bad Bash examples circulating online, centred on the most common mistakes like quoting and word splitting.

entry.title: Brendan Gregg
entry.summary: The blog and tools of the go-to expert on Linux performance and observability. Unlike general guides it gives kernel-level measurement and flame-graph methods.

entry.title: Command-line Fu
entry.summary: An archive of user-submitted UNIX one-liners ranked by vote — where you check whether a shortcut exists for a task.

entry.title: LinuxCommand.org
entry.summary: Teaches the command line from nothing and carries you into shell scripting; the home of "The Linux Command Line". Against a list of commands it follows a path — a sequenced course rather than a scattered cheat sheet.

entry.title: mempool.space
entry.summary: An explorer visualising Bitcoin’s pending transaction pool and the chain, runnable against your own node. Against other block explorers it adds fee estimation and a mempool view — it shows how congested the network is right now.

entry.title: Pure Bash Bible
entry.summary: A collection of ways to do things with Bash’s own facilities instead of calling external programs, which speeds scripts up markedly by removing sed and awk calls.

entry.title: Ryan’s Linux Tutorial
entry.summary: An introduction to Linux and Bash with exercises closing every section. Against LinuxCommand.org it is shorter and more drill-oriented — for getting through the basic commands quickly.

entry.title: Hiren's BootCD PE
entry.summary: A bootable Windows PE environment for systems that will not start, bundling disk cloning, password reset and data recovery in one image. The USB stick a sysadmin carries.

entry.title: ÇözümPark
entry.summary: A Turkish sysadmin community and article archive with real depth on Active Directory, Exchange and virtualisation — a rare resource for locally specific scenarios.

entry.title: ServiceDesk Simulator
entry.summary: Simulates working a real helpdesk queue — prioritisation, escalation, SLA tracking. It fills the practical gap that IT support courses leave theoretical.

entry.title: Cisco SG500-52P Kurulumu
entry.summary: First-time setup of one specific switch model, screenshot by screenshot — with the practical details the official manual skips.

entry.title: Cisco SG500 Serisi
entry.summary: Datasheets for the SG500 series comparing port counts, PoE budgets and stacking support — the model differences you need when buying second-hand.

entry.title: Active@ Disk Image
entry.summary: Takes and restores sector-level disk images. Unlike file backup it copies everything bit for bit, operating system and boot record included.

entry.title: Packet Tracer & Laboratuvarlar
entry.summary: The Packet Tracer download plus lab files, letting you practise VLAN, OSPF and ACL configuration without buying switches and routers.

entry.title: NetAcad Ağ Kursları (Türkçe)
entry.summary: The Turkish catalogue of Cisco networking courses, with free entry-level classes that award badges. Turkish-language networking training is not easy to find locally.

entry.title: Windows 11 Tam Rehber
entry.summary: A guide walking the whole of Windows 11’s settings, reaching into group policy and registry tweaks. A quick reference on the user-support side.
